name: Candy's
blurb: The Pali Hill institution. Still the best-known place on the hill, which is not a compliment they ever wanted.
description: A 1970s Persian-influenced cafe on Pali Hill that has outlasted almost everything around it. Order the walnut pastry; the sandwiches are the sleeper.

name: The Bombay Presidency
blurb: Fifty-one ingredients, one biryani, and a queue that forms before it opens.
description: A North Indian restaurant in a bungalow off Carter Road, famous for a single mutton kacchi biryani that reputedly involves 51 ingredients. Sunday lunch is the institution.

name: Mount Mary Steps
blurb: A climb of maybe a hundred steps, and then the whole Marine Drive arc laid out in front of you.
description: A steep set of concrete steps climbing St. Mary's Church to a terrace that looks straight down the western seafront. The light at about an hour before sunset is the whole point.

name: Bandra Fort
blurb: A 1738 fort with a sea view and almost no crowd after 11am.
description: Castella de Aguada, a Portuguese fortification from 1738 whose name still gets mispronounced. Ruins, a beach, and a wall high enough to see the Bandra-Worli sea link.

name: St. Francis of Assisi Church
blurb: An 1841 church, usually empty, five minutes from the sea.
description: The 1841 church at the foot of Mount Mary, a declared heritage monument with Goan and Portuguese elements. Empty on weekday mornings, which is exactly when you want it.

name: Mehboob Circus
blurb: An art-deco garden where Mumbai does its evening laps.
description: A 1930s garden ringed by art-deco bungalows, used every evening for walking, badminton, dogs and tai chi. Entry is through an art gallery, so you pay whatever is showing unless the gate is open.

name: Bandra Reclamation Promenade
blurb: A flat, planted, three-kilometre walk that a person built out of reclaimed land.
description: A wide artificial causeway that a city built out of nothing and then planted. Joggers at dawn, sea spray in the evening, and a very long walk when you want one.

name: Bandra Bus Depot Shacks
blurb: Shacks under the flyover beside the bus depot. Open late, cash only, worth building your evening around.
description: The line of shacks that appears under the flyover beside the western express highway when the buses stop. Bhendi baoli, kheema, butter chicken and a very cold beer, served off a cart, on plastic, and it is the best meal of the trip.

name: Bademi
blurb: A 1926 Parsi cafe. The berry pulao is why you came.
description: A Parsi cafe from 1926 that stayed open through Parsi New Year while half the city was elsewhere. The berry pulao is the argument for lunch here.

name: Juhu Beach
blurb: Long, wide, and crowded on weekends. Walk it at seven in the morning and the city is yours.
description: A beach that was dirtier and less crowded until it wasn't, and is now either perfect or unbearable depending on the day. Sunday afternoons have a flea market along the promenade. Do not swim: the water is not safe and the lifeguards will tell you so.

name: Prithvi Theatre
blurb: A 200-seat courtyard theatre. Cheap tickets, good writing, book ahead.
description: A courtyard theatre behind Prithvi Cafe that runs Marathi and Hindi plays, new writing, and an annual street festival. Tickets are cheap and the courtyard is small, so book a few days out.

name: Siddhivinayak Temple
blurb: Go at six in the morning or accept the queue. There is no third option.
description: The most-visited temple in Mumbai, and on a Tuesday or Thursday it is genuinely unmanageable. Go at opening, or not at all. The darshan queue is a separate, longer queue.

name: Kala Ghoda Arts District
blurb: Galleries on one plateau. Pick two, not eleven, and sit on the steps in between.
description: A square kilometre of galleries, studios and architecture on a single plateau. Do not try to see it all: pick two galleries, the Jehangir if you must, and sit on the steps of the National Gallery.

name: Jhangir Art Gallery
blurb: A 1952 gallery with a famous facade. The building is as good as the hang.
description: A 1952 modernist block, then a controversial blue-and-yellow dragon on the facade, now a serious contemporary space. The architecture and the gift shop are half the point.

name: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus
blurb: A working station that is also a World Heritage Site. Go at nine, before the commuters.
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and a working railway station, both at once. The stone carving is best first thing in the morning when the concourse is empty.

name: National Gallery of Modern Art, Mumbai
blurb: India's first public art gallery, in a converted warehouse. Cheap, cool, closed Wednesdays.
description: A kerosene-fountain warehouse made into India's first public art gallery, in the Fort precinct beside the CSMVS. Cheap, cool, and almost always quiet. Closed on Wednesdays, which catches people out.

name: Dr. Bhau Daji Lad City Museum
blurb: The city's decorative arts, in an 1872 building that is itself the exhibit.
description: The old Victoria and Albert Museum, in an 1872 Renaissance-revival building, holding the city's decorative arts. The building is the exhibit. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.

name: Haji Ali Dargah
blurb: A 1431 shrine on an islet. Wednesday sunset means qawwali.
description: A 1431 shrine on an islet, reached by causeway, at high tide almost unreachable. Every Wednesday is qawwali, from sunset, and it is one of the loudest, most beautiful things in the city.

name: Mahalaxmi Racecourse
blurb: Free to enter on race days, and a wide green walk whatever the result.
description: A horse-racing track that has been here since 1798 and is one of the few large open greens in the city. Admission is free on race days and the walk across it is the point.

name: Akshardham Temple
blurb: A 2013 temple, free, and the only truly calm one you will visit in Mumbai.
description: A 2013 Swaminarayan complex with a hand-carved wooden mandap that took seven years to build. Free, immaculate, and genuinely calm in a way most temples are not. Closed on Tuesdays.

name: Versova Village Jetty Walk
blurb: The fishing village where the catch still comes up the beach by hand. Go early, go respectfully.
description: The old Koli fishing village where Koli fishermen still land their catch, with women carrying it up the beach for the auction. Go with a local guide or on your own with respect. No photography of the fish auction without asking.

name: Crawford Market
blurb: Art Deco, still wholesale underneath, and the best produce in the city downstairs.
description: A 1934 Art Deco market over a wooden wholesale market, once the city's only source of imported fruit. Now a food hall and a produce market, still loud, still crowded, and the fruit on the ground floor is the cheap part.

name: Cafe Lota
blurb: A tiny cottage in a Fort lane, with bottle walls and a weekday calm.
description: A tiny Goa Villa cottage in a lane off MG Road, run by the Mario Miranda family, with a garden of old bottles in the walls. Go on a weekday; at weekends the lane is a queue.

name: Studio Pottery Session
blurb: Three hours at a wheel, a slightly lopsided result, and a studio that fires it for you.
description: A three-hour wheel session in a Bandra studio. You will make something slightly lopsided and take it home, and the studio will glaze and fire it if you come back next week. A good rainy-monsoon plan.

name: Shyamvan Nature Park
blurb: A wetland on reclaimed land, boardwalks, waders in winter, and almost no tourists.
description: A reclaimed-land wetland behind a housing colony, with boardwalks over marshland and a large bird population including migratory waders in winter. Free, quiet, and genuinely not on most itineraries.

name: Elephanta Caves
blurb: A ferry, a cliff-face of 500-year-old carvings, and a 17:30 boat home.
description: Rock-cut cave temples on an island an hour by ferry, with a 6m Trimurti that is the single most impressive thing in the Maharashtra interior. The boats stop running when the monsoon is out, and the last return is 17:30. Do not miss it.

name: Kanheri Caves
blurb: 109 Buddhist caves in a national park. Free, silent, forty minutes from Bandra.
description: 109 Buddhist caves cut into a basalt escarpment inside a national park, of which 14 are chaityas and the rest viharas. Free, deeply peaceful, and most people do not know they are 40 minutes away.

name: BKC Walk
blurb: A planted 900m spine through a business district, because nobody built on it.
description: A 900-metre landscaped spine between the BKC towers that the city's planners planted precisely because nobody wanted to build a mall on it. Joggers, office crowds at lunch, and a genuine green strip in a business district.

name: Bandra West Bungalow Walk
blurb: Ten people, a local historian, and the bungalows of Pali Hill explained properly.
description: A guided walk through the surviving art-deco and Portuguese bungalows of Pali Hill and Bandra Reclamation, with a local historian who can actually explain why a house faces the way it does. Ten people maximum, and it is the best three hours you will spend in Bandra.

name: Khar Dosa
blurb: Three decades on the same corner, and the food awards to match.
description: A South Indian place that has been on the same Khar corner for three decades and has won every food award in the city, including the one it does not talk about. Dosas are cooked to order and the filter coffee is the second reason.

name: Dharavi Community Walk
blurb: Run by the community, for the community, with a booking fee that goes to the guides.
description: A resident-led walk through a leather workshop, a pottery lane and a rooftop, run by the community association rather than outside it. The booking fee goes to the guides. Photography of residents is not permitted without asking each person.

name: Sea Princess Promenade
blurb: A wall on the reclamation, a drink, and the sea link coming on. No booking needed.
description: Not a club but a viewpoint: the reclamation edge where people sit on the wall and drink, with the Worli sea link lighting up in the middle distance. Cheap, outdoors, no booking.

name: Bal Gangadhar Temple
blurb: A 400-year-old stone Ganapati temple, saved from a name fight, never crowded.
description: A 400-year-old Ganapati temple that the 2004 name-changing dispute preserved by becoming a listed heritage monument. Small, stone, and far less crowded than any temple in the city centre.

name: Mithi River Walk
blurb: A river the city is un-concreting, with herons on the banks and dolphins past the estuary.
description: A dead river the city is slowly un-concreting, and the walk along it is the clearest example of that happening. Dolphins in the estuary, herons on the banks, and it is ten minutes from Powai station.

name: Yalga Gaaman Maharashtrian Thali
blurb: The thali has not changed since it opened, and the Mali wadi behind it is still standing.
description: A hole-in-the-wall doing a thali that has not changed since it opened, in an East Indian Mali wadi that still exists behind it. Ask for the fish thali if the fish is good that day, which it often is.

name: Colaba Causeway
blurb: A 19th-century main street, closed to cars on Sunday, with the best people-watching in Mumbai.
description: The last colonial-era main street, closed to traffic on Sunday. Bookshops, a Afghan bakery, a Knesset Eliyahoo synagogue, and the best people-watching in the city. Sunday afternoon is when it belongs.

name: Monsoon Gallery
blurb: A small video and photography gallery in a Bandra bungalow. Free, quiet, and rain-proof.
description: A small contemporary gallery in a Bandra bungalow, with a bias toward Indian video and photography work. Free, unhurried, and it will happily show you the video room if the rain starts.

name: Blue Frog Live Music
blurb: Live bands in a converted mill. Book ahead, or skip it on a weekend.
description: Two and a half hours of live bands in a converted textile mill, on a Wednesday or Thursday when the room is reliably full and the queue for a table is the real barrier. Book, or skip it entirely on a Friday.

name: Girgaon Ganpati Festival
blurb: A month of pandals that only exists in the monsoon. Immersion on day ten.
description: A pandal street each year, and a month and a half of installation that takes over the whole neighbourhood. It only exists in the monsoon, so a plan built in June may simply be gone by September. The idol is immersed on the tenth day at ten in the evening.

name: Mani Bhavan, Gandhi Smriti Sangrahalaya
blurb: An 1836 mansion where Quit India was launched, and a tour that explains why it matters.
description: The 1836 mansion where Gandhi spent five years as a law student and where the Quit India movement was launched from a room you can walk into. Small, quiet, and the guided tour is what makes it. Closed Mondays and Tuesdays.
